newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end down in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end down in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed lower on Monday in thin trading as investors took profits, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.11 pct to 107.48
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.18 pct at 107.14
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.02 pct to 109.15
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.24 pct to 106.54
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 107.14
Volume including Makams was an extremely low 42 million shekels.

"The market has reached equilibrium and activity was extremely low today. There are no buyers, no sellers and no volume," said Roy Meir of Simodan Brokerage House, adding that he expected the market to remain stable in the near term.

"Long CPI-linked bonds (10 to 15 years) were today's main losers. These bonds had risen sharply in the last few weeks and investors took profits today," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI).
After last week's interest rate cut, yields on long CPI-linked bonds fell below four percent.

"It appears that yields will not fall any further in the coming days," the FIBI trader said. "The rise of the dollar today also added to investors' fears that the Bank of Israel will not reduce the rates again in the near term as the rise of the dollar might lead to higher inflation."

After the Israeli cabinet adopted a plan on Wednesday to widen the exchange rate band and adjust its diagonal rate, the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent.
The FIBI trader said unlinked bonds and Makams closed almost unchanged. "With yields of 12.5 percent and inflation expectations of 8.5 percent these bonds are less attractive," he said.

Dollar-linked bonds were today's main gainers, rising sharply following the sharp decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency. "Dollar-linked bonds are expected to continue rising on Tuesday," Meir said.
But traders noted that volume in dollar-linked bonds was only 1.8 million shekels.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed on Monday at 3.4840 shekels to the dollar against 3.4370 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.48 shekels)
